ai.description: *Calotes emma* grows to 12 cm. It is olive-brown with dark lateral stripes and a bright red-spotted throat in males. Distinctive features include a prominent nuchal crest and long, slender limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Calotes emma* is best identified by the presence of a distinct, black, comma-shaped patch located immediately in front of the tympanum, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Forest Garden Lizard inhabits primary and secondary evergreen forests, often found in dense vegetation or along forest edges at elevations up to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Forest Garden Lizard is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on tree trunks or low branches to regulate its body temperature before actively hunting for insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calotes emma* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 4–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between May and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Calotes emma* occurs in Northeast India (e.g., Assam, Meghalaya) and the Andaman Islands, typically inhabiting tropical forests from lowlands up to 1,500 meters.
